title: A lifecycle declaration -- states and the transitions between them, as DATA
description: A folder can never force a decision; a column can. This document declares the states work may be in, and every passage between them with its owner, its exit criterion, and the door or guard that governs it. It carries no behaviour: nothing here branches, fetches or runs. An interpreter reads it and refuses what it does not declare -- which is why a transition that was never declared cannot be violated, and why declaring one is the whole cost of a new rule.

defers.description: This state holds work deliberately NOT being done now (ADR-025 decision 8). A card in it may name `due_when`, the trigger that makes it due; one that does is reported the moment its trigger holds, and one that does not is counted -- a deferral with no trigger is an abandonment that has not said so yet.

spends.description: Work SPENDS its declared appetite while it stands in this state (ADR-020 amendment 2). The spend of a record is the sum of its stays in such states, read from its own passages: a record not yet bet has spent nothing, a record that closed stops spending, and a record parked on purpose does not spend while it waits. A lifecycle that marks no state keeps the older reading -- the whole life of the record -- and the reading says which it took.

closed.description: This state holds work that is FINISHED (ADR-025 decision 13). The board shows it as a count and its most recent few, by the host's number, and the archive passage starts here: a project's age never grows the surface anyone reads to work.

door.description: A passage no machine may make. The named party must accept it, and the acceptance is recorded exactly as an install approval is -- one mechanism, two subjects.

computed.description: A passage DECIDED BY A MACHINE, and the reference that decides it (ADR-020 decision 8). What is machine-decidable is never set by hand: a state a principal could type means only that somebody said so, and the evidence beside it becomes decoration. This and `door` are the two modes a passage may declare and they are exclusive -- a passage that declared both would be claiming a judgement nobody may automate and a computation nobody may make.

proof.description: A typed reference about the card standing at this passage, resolved through the same open registry a criterion's proof is resolved through -- so a condition is declared in exactly the grammar a proof is declared in, and the interpreter that reads it holds no condition of its own. The GRAMMAR of a reference has one home, on the criterion that declares one; nothing here restates it, because a shape declared twice drifts while both copies go on reading as correct. What a reference that cannot be read means is settled where it is resolved: no reading, therefore no passage -- never a pass.

when.description: A DECLARED bypass (ITIL's pre-approved standard change): this passage is open only to cards whose field holds this value. Bypass by declaration, never by omission -- a card is still written.
